newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW-Randgold looks beyond Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Randgold looks beyond Bre-X.

text.p: South Africa-based minerals exploration firm Randgold Resources said on Thursday the effects of the Bre-X gold scandal would not haunt new listing of mining firms indefinitely.

The firm earlier listed in London with its offer price set at $16.50 a share -- well down on the expected $18-23 -- and the size of the offer five million shares instead of the expected seven million.
The firm said it had not met its initial ambitious targets in part due to the fall-out of the Bre-X debacle, where a Canadian firm vastly overstated the potential wealth of an Indonesian gold find.
Randgold Resources chief executive Mark Bristow told Reuters by telephone from London that the market was still suffering from the effects of the scandal, but he did not expect them to last for long.
"I don't think it will be a couple of years, these things have happened through the years and there is always space for good quality growth companies," he said.
Bristow said he was satisfied with the listing outcome, which came amid other adverse market conditions, like the low gold price.
"I am very satisfied that the team has got this far in this time, he said.
"The gold price went down below $340 an ounce. It was significant and generally the perception in the market is sensitive to something like that."

He said the $82.5 million proceeds from the offering would go towards funding the capital expenditure programme at the firm's Syama gold mine in Mali and repayment of a loan assumed when it bought Syama last year.
It would also be used to develop the Loulo mine in Mali and pay for a bankable feasibility study for the Golden Ridge project in Tanzania.
"In addition, it will fund our ongoing exploration programme," Bristow said.
He said the company now had a market capitalisation of $327 million -- based on the offer price.
